newsitem.title: UK: Benetton launches Food Summit ad campaign.
newsitem.headline: Benetton launches Food Summit ad campaign.

text.p: Benetton, the Italian clothing company known for its controversial advertisements, said on Thursday it would jointly sponsor an advertising campaign with the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) to promote the forthcoming World Food Summit in Rome.

Benetton, in a press release issued from its headquarters in Ponzano, Italy, said the newspaper and poster ad campaign would feature a wooden spoon on a white background to symbolise man's relationship with food -- or with hunger.

The ad, created by Oliviero Toscani, will be published in newspapers in Italy, France, Belgium, Britain, Holland and Spain on November 13, the opening day of the Food Summit. The outdoor poster campaign, which will also run in Chile, Brazil, the Caribbean and Mexico, will begin on November 1 and increase as the start of the summit draws nearer.
The summit will run from November 13 to 17.
A spokeswoman for Benetton in London declined to give the cost of the ad campaign.
Benetton said the ad was created in response to a request by the Food and Agriculture Organisation that Italy's top businesses show an interest in the problem of world hunger.
Benetton said the ad is one in a series of cooperative projects it has undertaken with major humanitarian organisations, including Caritas, the Red Cross and SOS Racisme.

Benetton, which recently drew fire for a billboard advertisement featuring a black horse and a white horse mating, began its controversial advertising campaigns in 1989. Previous posters have shown a white baby being breast-fed by a black woman, bodies stamped "HIV positive" and a nun and a priest kissing.
